title: Biplanar line graphs are 9-colourable, and biplanar graphs have independence ratio above 2/21 (Earth-Moon problem)
description:
Two results on the Earth-Moon problem (the chromatic number of biplanar / thickness-2 graphs; known bounds 9 ≤ χ ≤ 12).

(1) Every biplanar line graph is 9-colourable. If the line graph L(H) of a loopless multigraph H is biplanar, then its fractional chromatic number and its chromatic number are at most 9, so no line graph can be a 10-chromatic biplanar graph. The proof reduces the statement to 22 explicit 28-vertex line graphs, each proved non-biplanar by a machine-checked Lean 4 theorem (LRAT certificates with Kuratowski witness clauses and verified symmetry breaking). Also: biplanar joins K_s ∨ H with s ≥ 5 have fractional chromatic number at most 9, sharp for K_5 ∨ C_8^2.

(2) Every biplanar graph on n vertices has an independent set of size greater than 2n/21, answering Král's Problem 4 from the Barbados Graph Theory Workshop 2018 (c > 1/12), as a corollary of Abiad-Kumar-Pragada (arXiv:2609.00210).

Includes proofs, the Lean 4 package with all 22 certified instances and their witness data, a rebuild tool that regenerates and re-checks every certificate, an independent audit, enumeration scripts and logs. Produced by an AI research framework under human direction; reviewed adversarially by AI models of three families (not peer review); not peer-reviewed. Every claim carries its verification status in the README.

v1.1.0 adds a Lean 4 check of the two finite enumerations behind the reduction to the 22 graphs (Biplanar.Enum.five_not_biplanar and Biplanar.Enum.seven_not_biplanar; every case generated and certified inside Lean), so the whole finite part of the line-graph theorem is machine-checked, together with the scripts and logs of the uncertified evidence computations (circulant joins, Patil corpus census, local search) and a fix to the rebuild tool.
